I have a love/hate relationship with Paradox, so I was understandably on the fence about this one, but it has totally blown away my expectations. It's polished, runs smoothly, and has so much depth that you'll spend hours on it before you even get the hang of colonization, if you're a reader.

For a multiplatform title, I was not expecting this level of finish, even at this price point, because outfits like Firaxis have been unable to even come close at even higher price points.

If you like the epic scale of GalCiv, the feel of Sins, and wish both were slapped together into a game that feels like it was written for Linux, then give Stellaris a try.

Anyone that's played this, how different is it from other paradox titles? Is it some sort of combination of previous titles or is it completely different from all existing titles?

I haven't done my research into the game yet, but I've been afraid that this game would mostly be a graphical mod of one of their other games á la Civ: Beyond Earth.

You know how some people complained that some of the mechanics in Civ4 literally did not do what they said, that some options were pointless, and that some aspects of the game were tedious for the specific purpose of hiding that fact?

Firaxis took that and made Civilization: Revolutions. It made everything slicker, faster, and somewhat simpler. It also didn't really fix any of the actual things people complained about.

Now imagine CivRev, with the mechanics from 4 people actually liked, and with the more tedious aspects toned down instead of ported right over.

Stellaris is like "Crusader Kings II: Revolutions" - a slimmer, slicker, easier to understand game. It therefor is not quite as rich. But I can tell you, I have over a hundred hours in Civ5 and I have never won even a single Normal difficulty level game of Crusaders Kings II.

Stellaris is the game I wanted CKII to be.

(And I would not say CivBE was just a reskin - far from it. It breaks lots of things that worked perfectly fine in Civ5. And while it innovates in some mechanics, they are so different they don't feel like Civ. It was a decent game - they just shouldn't have called it Civ.
